Recent findings suggest that apple marketing SVP Greg Joswiak stated today that the number of iPhone Duo-ready apps on the App Store is twice what it was when Apple last reported the figure. Here are the details.

While it was obvious that the number of iPhone Duo-ready apps would increase over time, their limited availability was a massive part of the conversation around early reviews and online commentary in the first days after the device rolled out.

That remarked, it was clear even from the early reviews that app updates were picking up promptly, with some reviewers having to rewrite or re-record parts of their coverage as more apps gained support for the device.

Earlier this month, Apple put a number to that progress when it unveiled it had surpassed 100,000 optimized apps.

Now, just 10 days later, that number has doubled, according to Apple’s senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing, Greg Joswiak. In a post on X, he touted that more than 200,000 apps are now optimized for iPhone Duo, adding that he is “excited by how quickly developers have embraced” the device.

According to recent reports, over 200,000 apps are now optimized for iPhone Duo! That number DOUBLED in just over a week.I’m excited by how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and I can’t wait to see what they build next.

Joswiak’s patch came on the same day that Apple released iOS 27.3 developer beta 2, which addresses two other common complaints from early iPhone Duo reviews: the lack of Face ID, and the inability to automatically lock the device when closing it.

  • For users in the UK, the patch brings over 10 distinct English voice options covering a wide range of regional cadences.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following a preview at Google I/O, Google is rolling out 66 fresh regional voices to the Gemini app on both Android and iOS today. The expansion introduces tailored voice options across U.S. English, U.K. English, Indian English, Hindi, Brazilian Portuguese, Indonesian, and Korean.

For users in the UK, the patch brings over 10 distinct English voice options covering a wide range of regional cadences. The lineup includes Geordie, Scouse, Brummie, Scottish, Welsh, Northern Irish, Modern RP, and Multicultural London English (MLE).

This might help reduce the issues that sometimes still occur when English accents, in particular, morph into a hybrid of Australian or even American that has been going on for a while with Gemini Live. We have not yet been able to test to confirm this has been resolved with the patch. As someone with a regional English accent, this extra representation with Gemini voices is quite welcome.

According to Google, these voices are tuned for natural pronunciation, pitch, and everyday local rhythm rather than exaggerated stereotypes. Because the focus is on cadence over slang, Gemini will sound like a local without filling its text responses with forced street slang. Once selected, your chosen voice carries across the entire app, applying to both Gemini Live conversations and standard text-to-speech playback when tapping the “Listen” icon on chat responses.

You can preview and select the new options today by tapping the three-dot menu inside Gemini Live, or by heading into the Gemini app settings and selecting “Gemini’s voice.” It’s worth noting that the voices aren’t explicitly labeled by city or region in the app menu, and Gemini isn’t programmed to self-identify which accent it is using if you ask it directly.

It has been revealed that instead, Google notes that locally rooted prompts about food, culture, or sport, such as asking for the best pub in Sheffield for a Sunday roast – my suggestion is not a pub; it’s Turnip & Thyme on Eccleshall Road, FWIW. Or another suggestion from significant G is where to find proper ingredients for a traditional Scouse stew; the manufacturer indicates these will naturally bring out the warmth and rhythm of the new dialects.

I’d suggest trying to ask where to get the best pattie and chips in Hull or where to get the best pint in Leeds (it’s Whitelocks).

  • Google notes people can use the navigation platform’s “Ask Maps” tool to build step-by-step trip itineraries and get real-time details about their route right when they pull up directions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google announced on Monday that it’s rolling out newly introduced Maps features that are designed to help people strategy trips and everyday tasks using AI. The firm is launching the ability for Maps to create trip itineraries and find appointments for users.

It has been revealed that the new features reflect a broader shift in how tech companies are positioning AI, which is less as a tool that just answers questions and more as an assistant that can complete tasks on consumers’ behalf. While many companies have released AI agents to complete these tasks, Google is working to bring that approach into a service that millions of people already use every day.

Google notes people can use the navigation platform’s “Ask Maps” tool to build step-by-step trip itineraries and get real-time details about their route right when they pull up directions.

Industry observers note that for example, you could use Ask Maps to plan a holiday shopping day trip or something more complex, like a three-day road trip featuring coastal hikes and oceanfront dining, Google says. You’ll get a day-by-day itinerary with insider tips and numbered map pins for every stop. Once you’re happy with your itinerary, you can share it with friends and family or export it to Google Docs on desktop.

When you’re ready to head out, you can use Ask Maps to reopen your itinerary or find the “itinerary” badge in your chat history. You’ll have access to real-time information, including traffic conditions, business hours, and a look at what the “vibe” is at your next stop, the company says. You could also adjust your schedule by asking Maps to do something like add a scenic viewpoint or lunch stop along your route. You can then tap any destination in your itinerary to get directions and navigate to your next stop.

Additionally, people can use Ask Maps to find beauty, pet care, auto, and home repair appointments online and call local businesses for you. For example, you could ask: “Find me a 4 p.m. nail appointment near me.” Ask Maps will then display open slots across nearby businesses.

The new agentic calling feature arrives as tech companies continue to introduce AI agents designed to handle time-consuming tasks, such as scheduling DMV appointments and making reservations. For example, Meta’s AI agent Muse recently gained the ability to call businesses on users’ behalf.

Google also announced that you can now use Ask Maps to rapidly find places on your lists by asking something like: “Which spots saved in my lists have availability for five people in the next 30 minutes?”.

Sources indicate that the tech giant says the fresh updates are starting to roll out on Monday on Android and iOS. As part of the news, Google announced that Ask Maps is expanding to 30 countries across Europe, including Spain, Germany, and the U.K.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 will feature a playable female character for the first time since the 2D games.

After 13 years of waiting, some GTA 6 fans are taking extra steps to play the game - from booking time off work, buying a console to play it on or even pretending they're halfway around the world to get early access.

Market intelligence firm Sensor Tower estimates, external GTA 6 has already generated $1.18bn (Â£894m) from 12 million pre-orders - although Rockstar has not confirmed this.

Despite the option to preload the 212GB game, Jennifer Holmes, chief executive of the London Internet Exchange, stated several UK internet providers including BT and Virgin Media had "increased capacity in anticipation of higher demand" ahead of launch.

But for some fans, simply having the game ready to play is not enough.

GTA 6 - all you need to know about Rockstar's blockbuster game.

Gamers have long been known to book time off work for major releases.

When Red Dead Redemption 2 released in October 2018, social media users were sharing aims to take the day off, with one analytics firm reportedly finding, external more people talking about calling in sick for it than any other game that year.

Similar conversations took place ahead of Cyberpunk 2077's release in December 2020, with fans discussing , externaltaking several days off to play.

GTA 6 is no exception, but it appears to characteristically be taking things to a whole upcoming level.

For the game's launch day, HR software tech giant BrightHR, external looked at absence data from more than 1.2 million employees from 70,000 businesses across the UK.

It found GTA was mentioned in 4.6% of time-off requests by employees. Throughout November and December, it said an estimated 83,000 days had been booked off for the game.

It has been revealed that according to the HR firm, one person put "latest GTA is coming out! I will be spending a week on the sofa in my pants!" as the reason for their leave request, while another noted: "play the new GTA - I've waited a billion years".

A third said in their request: "GTA Release - I'll put my notice in if this is denied.".

The manufacturer added it had no way of tracking if the requests had actually been approved by employers.

GTA 6 is set in a fictional state inspired by Florida, which has featured heavily in the game's marketing, including this promotional blimp.

Some places have even decided to lean into the trend by offering incentives around the game â including the US Army's 3rd Infantry Division based at Fort Stewart, Georgia.

It gave some active-duty soldiers a four-day pass to play the game when it is released in November, as long as they sign a reenlistment contract for a minimum of two years between 1 August and 12 November.

"The idea was to have a unique incentives programme that connects to what soldiers are interested in," public affairs officer for the division, Lieutenant Colonel Angel Tomko confirmed to the BBC in August.

"There are 130 soldiers eligible within the battalion, and 20 have selected this incentive as part of their reenlistment," she said at the time.

Aside from taking time off, some gamers have also been discussing a technical loophole which could give them valuable extra hours of play before it officially unlocks in their country.

Because GTA 6 will release at midnight local time in all regions, Upcoming Zealand will become one of the first places where it is available, due to it reaching midnight earliest because of its position near the international date line.

This has led to some investigating ways to "trick" their consoles into thinking they're based in the island country when they are in fact thousands of miles away.

According to Google Trends, searches for the "GTA 6 Newly introduced Zealand trick" have surged by more than 5,000% in the UK over the past month.

Games journalist Vic Hood said many gamers would be looking to play earlier to "get in on the action as soon as possible", as well as to prevent spoilers.

"As Fresh Zealand is 13 hours ahead of the UK, that's 13 hours of gameplay that has time to spread across the internet and potentially spoil some key story beats and in-game surprises," she noted.

"Took an extra day of paid time off when I found this out," one fan posted on Reddit on the trick.

It also means gamers would be playing the game at the much nicer time of 11:00 GMT, rather than having to stay up all night.

But another Xbox user shared caution on Reddit, noting that while the loophole had been exploited for many years for other game releases, GTA 6 "might be the game where Microsoft finally does something about this 'exploit'" - which could include banning players.

GTA 6's developers Rockstar and publishers Take Two Interactive have not commented on the loophole, and neither has Sony nor Microsoft.

Louise Wooldridge from analyst firm Ampere Analysis mentioned both Microsoft and Sony had "rules governing regional accounts and purchases" for the Xbox and PlayStation, adding that Sony's were "slightly more restrictive".

Players who choose to use the workaround could therefore risk breaching those terms and conditions and potentially face restrictions on their accounts or lose access to their digital games.

The hype for the game has taken over locations across the world, including Selfridges in London.

Some gamers will have to wait even longer than their console-playing counterparts to get their hands on GTA 6, as the game will not be available on PC at launch, similar to previous GTA releases.

"Spare a thought for the PC consumers who will have to live vicariously through others' YouTube videos and Twitch streams," gamer Stephen Finn told the BBC.

A PS5 now costs from Â£520, while the more powerful PS5 Pro is nearly Â£790.

Despite the hefty price tag, for some the temptation to join the community in playing what many have called the biggest game launch of the year, if not decade, has been too great.

#798. US tightens AI chip export controls to deter Chinese companies from accessing compute remotely

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (734 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

US tightens AI chip export controls to deter Chinese companies from accessing compute remotely

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (734 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Trump administration on Monday is preparing to roll out fresh export controls on AI chips and data centers outside the U.S., seeking to prevent companies, especially those in China, from getting past U.S.
  • Under the interim rule, the Commerce Department will require companies to get licenses to export, reexport, or transfer AI chips and servers to data centers anywhere in the world if they may provide compute to companies in China or other restricted countries.
  • The remote-access rules target companies based in the U.S.’s D:5 group of embargoed countries, which includes China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, and 18 others.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Trump administration on Monday is preparing to roll out fresh export controls on AI chips and data centers outside the U.S., seeking to prevent companies, especially those in China, from getting past U.S. export controls by remotely accessing AI infrastructure located in other countries.

Under the interim rule, the Commerce Department will require companies to get licenses to export, reexport, or transfer AI chips and servers to data centers anywhere in the world if they may provide compute to companies in China or other restricted countries.

The remote-access rules target companies based in the U.S.’s D:5 group of embargoed countries, which includes China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, and 18 others.

Sources indicate that the U.S. already has rules requiring chip companies to get a license to ship AI chips to companies based in, or owned by any business in, this group of countries.

“This new control is a logical extension of existing controls,” the interim rule reads. “These restrictions will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using U.S. advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors to train advanced SI models.”.

The move comes days after Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned amid a scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy linked to one of the chipmaker’s customers. The U.S. government has reportedly been wanting to put that customer, Megaspeed, on a special entity list, as it believes the company has been buying thousands of Nvidia chips to provide compute to Chinese businesses to get past existing export-control restrictions.

Reuters reported last week that Chinese AI companies are rushing to secure computing capacity overseas amid fears of tighter restrictions from the U.S.

The rule applies to data centers or any network that can supply over 12 million total processing performance (TPP), an export-control metric the U.S. uses to measure computing power. (Twelve million TPP roughly works out to the max computing power of about 750 Nvidia H100 or H200 chips.) The rule also covers indirect access through go-betweens or brokers, and exporters and data center operators are required to keep an eye on their customers’ ownership structures and activities to ensure they aren’t run by anyone from the D:5 group.

The rule also adds fresh licensing requirements for chip exports, reexports, or transfer of advanced semiconductors to Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, and Brazil. The Commerce Department stated it had included these as they “present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.” For these countries, however, the license requirements will not apply to chips “destined” for companies based in the U.S.

Existing data center operators providing services that fall under this newly introduced rule are required to get licenses within 90 days of the rule coming into effect.

Notably, the rule doesn’t apply to commercial recommendation systems, like those used in e-commerce or social media.

The rule also rescinds the Biden admin’s AI Diffusion Rule from January 2025, which sought to impose country-level limits on exports of advanced AI chips, and restrict transfers of certain powerful AI models. That May, the Trump administration stated it would throw out that framework, arguing that it added unnecessary restrictions on U.S. companies and the country’s allies.

“By making these changes, this IFR prevents the use of certain SI items in data centers and at a computing power level that can be used for training or running of advanced SI models,” the rule reads. “Access to such computing power can be used to train and run advanced SI models capable of supporting military- and intelligence-related activities that could threaten U.S. national security or foreign policy interests.”.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Health officials in Pennsylvania and Wisconsin announced two more measles deaths late last week, bringing the national tally of confirmed measles deaths this year to 10.
  • Wisconsin health officials stated the latest measles death—the second for the state—was in a child.
  • For all the states with deaths so far, health officials have noted that they’re the first deaths in decades.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Health officials in Pennsylvania and Wisconsin announced two more measles deaths late last week, bringing the national tally of confirmed measles deaths this year to 10. The total includes the deaths of at least four infants: two in Pennsylvania, one in New York, and one in Wisconsin.

Wisconsin health officials stated the latest measles death—the second for the state—was in a child. Pennsylvania’s health department did not reveal the age or other details of the latest death—the state’s seventh—besides revealing it was of an unvaccinated resident in Montour County. Overall, the seven deaths in Pennsylvania include two in Jefferson County, three in Lancaster County, and one in Mifflin, in addition to the new death in Montour. An eighth death was reported in Franklin County, but state health officials have not confirmed it.

For all the states with deaths so far, health officials have noted that they’re the first deaths in decades. Multiple outbreaks are underway across the country, pushing the national tally of cases to nearly 5,500 across 47 states and jurisdictions, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Pennsylvania’s case count alone is over 1,500, and Wisconsin is reporting nearly 650.

According to recent reports, with outbreaks that have been smoldering and flaring since last year, the US has reportedly lost its measles elimination status—as medical and public health experts have widely expected it would. A panel of experts for the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a regional branch of the World Health Organization, convened last week to review US measles data and assess its elimination status. The PAHO is set to announce its conclusion and the review’s other findings on Tuesday, November 17. But sources broke the news to The Wall Street Journal on Friday that the panel had found that the US had indeed lost its status.

An elimination status is determined by international health authorities after a country has gone more than 12 months without continuous spread of a virus. The status is lost when epidemiological and laboratory data indicate that a chain of transmission involving a viral strain with an identical genotype and lineage has continued uninterrupted for 12 months or longer.

The US earned its elimination status in 2000 after hard-fought vaccination campaigns over several decades. But US vaccination rates have slipped below protective levels in recent years, fueled by the rise of anti-vaccine rhetoric and vaccine misinformation from fierce anti-vaccine advocates, including current US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. As vaccination rates slipped, measles cases skyrocketed. The current case tally is the highest seen since 1991.

Recent findings suggest that in reporting the PAHO’s determination, the Journal quoted Noel Brewer, chair of an independent US committee who presented findings about the country’s measles outbreaks to PAHO, on the country’s lamentable status: “Runaway measles outbreaks in the United States, as well as the needless deaths, are all due to low measles vaccination coverage. We’ve gotten comfortable letting children be stopped by a deadly disease and die from it.”.

The US Department of Health and Human Services did not immediately respond to requests to comment about the loss of the elimination status or to answer a question about how anti-vaccine rhetoric and misinformation, including that from Kennedy, has contributed.

Medical and public health experts continue to sharply criticize Kennedy’s and the Trump administration’s poor handling of the ongoing severe outbreaks. The CDC has not held press briefings in efforts to halt the vaccine-preventable illness and promote vaccination. Instead, Kennedy reportedly ordered the CDC to remove measles death data, and the CDC director declined to approve an urgent health alert about the life-threatening risks of measles during pregnancy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bloomberg reports that Apple lifer Corey Fugman will replace Jennifer Bailey as the head of the Apple Pay and Wallet division. Here are the details.

A few months ago, Bloomberg reported that Jennifer Bailey, Apple’s head of Apple Pay and Wallet, who had led Apple Pay since its launch in 2014, would retire in October.

At the time, Apple’s services boss Eddy Cue stated internally that the company would announce its succession strategy before her transition at the end of October, and that she would “continue to be available to support the transition in an advisory role.”.

October came and went without any public announcement on that front. Today, however, Bloomberg reported that Apple has tapped Corey Fugman, “a 26-year company veteran as the new head of its payment service and digital wallet unit.”.

According to his LinkedIn profile, Fugman joined Apple in September 2000 as Merchandising Manager for Apple Retail and has held several leadership positions since then, including overseeing Apple Card and Apple Cash from 2019 to 2021.

Most recently, he served as Senior Director of Apple Pay and Wallet, a position he has held since November 2021.

With the fresh job, Fugman inherits a crucial tap-to-pay business, which is estimated to generate billions of dollars a year. It handles tens of billions of transactions annually across more than 90 markets, with Apple taking a percentage.

In a recent development, the division also includes the Apple Card, which is transitioning from a partnership with Goldman Sachs Group Inc. to JPMorgan Chase & Co. Fugman has been highly involved with the shift to Chase, which is still ongoing, the people stated.

The report notes that Fugman will report to Cue, and reaffirms that Bailey “will remain a consultant in the coming months,” echoing Cue’s earlier comments about her role in the transition.

Finally, Bloomberg adds that while Apple has undergone several leadership changes in recent months, including John Ternus replacing Tim Cook as CEO, Cue’s responsibilities have expanded considerably.

In addition to overseeing services such as Apple TV, Apple Music, Maps, and iCloud, Cue has recently taken charge of the App Store and Health following Jeff Williams’ departure as Chief Operating Officer and Phil Schiller’s decision to step down from overseeing the App Store.

Microsoft outage cause revealed: It was a perfect storm of problems

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (712 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that you're probably aware that Microsoft 365, the popular suite of products that includes Outlook, suffered a massive global outage last week.
  • Aside from wondering when their email would be working again, the number one question on everyone's mind was what in the world happened to keep Microsoft 365 down for so long?
  • According to recent reports, now, we know.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that you're probably aware that Microsoft 365, the popular suite of products that includes Outlook, suffered a massive global outage last week. In fact, it was the worst outage of the year, by a sizable margin. The problem took the computer giant roughly 24 hours, over the course of two business days, to get everything back up and running.

Aside from wondering when their email would be working again, the number one question on everyone's mind was what in the world happened to keep Microsoft 365 down for so long?

According to recent reports, now, we know. In a statement shared with customers and on X, Microsoft explained there were actually three causes, which created a perfect storm.

First, a bug caused servers to become unresponsive in specific conditions; second, an issue with Microsoft Teams increased server traffic and created those conditions; and third, many additional servers were already offline from an unrelated issue.

Recent findings suggest that as Microsoft explained, on their own, neither issue would have caused such a large-scale problem. However, together, well, they kept one of the world's biggest tech companies scrambling for two days to fix their service.

In a social media post published on X, Microsoft's EVP of Copilot, Agents, and Platform Charles Lamanna explained the situation in detail.

According to Lamanna, a "latent defect" resulted in the firm's servers becoming "overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions." The defect that caused the problem was introduced to Microsoft's systems during a July 2026 update as part of a fix for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers.

For months, as Lamanna described it, the matter went undetected, and it didn't cause any problems under normal load during Microsoft's testing process.

Sources indicate that the second problem occurred when a surge in server load set off the defect. Lamanna says that Microsoft maintains two independent network gateway systems for Microsoft 365 to handle outages and disruptions. However, 15 hours before the global Microsoft 365 outage, Teams "failed over" from the alternative networking gateway to the primary one, which supports Exchange Online. The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

This wouldn't usually cause a problem, except for the new defect introduced by the July upgrade.

Finally, Microsoft's servers weren't operating at 100 percent at the time. According to Lamanna, it just so happened that nearly 14 percent of the server capacity for the networking gateway was out of service "due to an unrelated glitch from the previous day.".

According to recent reports, again, normally, this would have been routine maintenance. The service would still have sufficient capacity to work as normal.

All three issues occurring at once led to disaster.

"Taken together, the increased load and the reduced server capacity, caused the network gateway to encounter the latent bug from July," Lamanna writes. "This caused requests to build up until servers ultimately stopped responding. This occurred during the peak window of traffic in the United States.".

Recovery from the outage also took much longer than usual because servers were "immediately overwhelmed by waiting traffic and became unresponsive again." In addition, Microsoft was unable to roll back the code because the bug dated back to July. So, Microsoft essentially had to develop a patch within that short timeframe, which returned the code to its previous "good state.".

The entire explanation from Microsoft is actually quite an interesting read and shows that no matter how big the tech giant is, massive tech complications can still occur. Readers can check out Lamanna's entire post on X; Microsoft enterprise customers can also learn more in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center.

Recent findings suggest that microsoft has since apologized for the outage. Businesses affected by the downtime can also file a claim with the manufacturer for credits due to the downtime.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Amazon-owned audiobook service Audible is turning to AI to help listeners find their next book. The tech giant on Monday launched a new “audio discovery” feature that provides a brief overview of a book’s themes and a summary of what readers liked about it, as well as commentary from an Audible editor or an author, in addition to playing the narrated sample.

The overview audio itself is generated using AI, and the commentary is pulled from recordings of past Audible interviews, the company says.

The idea is that this type of expanded introduction to a story could help users decide what to listen to next, particularly when they’re on the go and don’t have time to scroll through comments or reviews.

The feature follows last month’s launch of a handful of AI tools that let people engage more with the story, interact with characters, or catch up with the help of recaps. These features have come as Audible faces fresh competition in the audiobooks market, namely from Spotify, which introduced audiobook listening hours as part of its paid subscriptions. That service expanded last month to over 180 markets.

In a recent development, audible’s new feature takes a cue from how Amazon is already using AI to help people shop: On the Amazon storefront, AI can summarize buyers’ product reviews so shoppers can get a quick sense of what people had to say, as well as the pros and cons of a particular item. In Audible’s case, it’s pulling information about what people liked about the book from publicly available reviews.

But such a feature could limit owners’ exposure to negative reviews if the AI only pulls information from those that offer positive remarks. (Further testing will be needed to see if this is the case, of course.).

Audible says the overviews will also draw on other publicly available materials, like synopses and metadata.

The feature will initially be available for select English-language titles in the U.S., and will arrive alongside new personalized collections based on users’ listening taste that could help them find other books.

In a recent development, the tech giant’s other recent AI features, Recaps and the interactive “Ask a Question” tool, are also now expanding to more U.S. titles, and will become more broadly available in December. These features will only be available to customers who have purchased a title or who have access to the book as part of their Audible membership, the company mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that “Picking your next listen should feel like getting a tip from a friend,” mentioned Andy Tsao, Audible’s chief product and analytics officer, in a statement. “With audio discovery, you’ll get a quick audio take on why the title might be right for you from our editors, fellow listeners, or even the author. Some of the best listening experiences are those rare finds or hidden gems, and we want to make those great discoveries happen more often and more easily,” he added.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, I don’t go into any given week at WIRED assuming I’ll be thinking much about extramarital affairs. But last week, they were the only thing on my mind.

According to recent reports, these thoughts, of course, were prompted by Jensen Huang. In the span of a few completely insane days, the billionaire CEO and cofounder of Nvidia went from being a globally influential Silicon Valley executive to a lesson in exactly what not to do if you want to keep your job, and the extraordinary power that comes with it. It’s a damn mess—for Huang and his family, sure, but also for Nvidia, the AI industry the tech giant is instrumental in powering, and the entirety of the global economy.

WIRED’s senior correspondent Lauren Goode has spent years reporting on Nvidia and Huang, including interviewing the man himself on multiple occasions. She also spent last week breaking news about his downfall, despite being in Europe on vacation. (Sorry, Lauren. You can have those PTO days back.) So at the end of a very long week for WIRED’s newsroom, I called Lauren to talk about what she makes of Huang’s ouster, what it means for AI, and where this all goes next. We also made a bet about Huang’s future—one involving a meal he recently made semi-famous.

This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

Building AI that can work across the enterprise

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 28 min read (5642 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Technologyreview

⏱️ ~28 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that for years, enterprises have approached AI as a series of discrete experiments.
  • For Thorsten Leiduck, SVP and global head of SAP Business AI Platform Ecosystem, that shift begins with treating AI as an enterprise platform rather than a collection of disconnected projects.
  • That foundation also determines which AI applications are worth pursuing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that for years, enterprises have approached AI as a series of discrete experiments. Now, as AI agents begin to move into the workflows that run the business, that model is starting to look inadequate. Organizations moving from isolated pilots toward AI agents and autonomous workflows are confronting a deeper challenge: rethinking how data, business processes, governance, and people fit together, turning AI from a collection of tools into part of the enterprise operating model.

For Thorsten Leiduck, SVP and global head of SAP Business AI Platform Ecosystem, that shift begins with treating AI as an enterprise platform rather than a collection of disconnected projects. “AI is absolutely dependent on the data foundation,” he indicates, arguing that companies need a connected, semantically rich layer that reflects their business before they can reliably deploy AI across processes. The stakes also change as AI moves into mission-critical workflows. For some everyday applications, “80% might be good enough,” he says, but in areas such as supply chains or financial close, that level of accuracy is “a very terrible result.”.

That foundation also determines which AI applications are worth pursuing. Satinder Pal Singh, associate VP North America for SAP BAIP and SAP AI Strategy at Infosys, frames AI agents as “digital coworkers” and recommends evaluating potential use cases through three lenses: impact, feasibility, and scalability. Companies should identify where an agent can move meaningful business metrics, determine whether their data and talent can support the use case, and then establish whether successful applications can be replicated. “A pilot that can't scale is just an experiment,” he says.

Scaling also brings governance into sharper focus. Clear policies, access controls, monitoring, and oversight are necessary to ensure agents remain trustworthy and aligned with business requirements. “The absence of governance doesn't speed up AI adoption,” Singh says. “It creates a risk backlog” that can ultimately force a more disruptive stop and audit.

Those considerations will become more key as AI agents take on more responsibilities as digital coworkers. Both executives see a future in which agentic systems coordinate work across applications, while customer-specific knowledge graphs and governed data become critical enterprise assets. For Singh, the longer-term opportunity is a shift from AI as a productivity tool to “AI as a decision-making partner,” helping leaders understand what is happening, anticipate what comes next, and determine how to respond.

It's becoming clear that, unlike past ways of automation, AI requires a real mindset shift. Put simply, the technology can't simply be added into an enterprise's existing toolkit. It requires a complete reconfiguration of what's inside and how it's used.

Sources indicate that satinder: Absolutely, Megan. And, if anything, the picture sharpens when you look at, specifically, at agentic AI. Infosys and HFS research surveyed over 500 global 2,000 enterprises and found only 14% have successfully scaled AI. Eighty-six percent remain in early exploration, proof of concept, or fragmented pilot phases. For a technology at the top of every boardroom agenda for two years, that's a striking failure rate. And at the core of that 86% is what I would describe as AI as a department trap.

#788. LangChain raises $300m at a $3bn valuation to help companies run AI agents

LangChain raises $300m at a $3bn valuation to help companies run AI agents

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (364 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • LangChain, which makes tools for building and running AI agents, has raised $300m at a $3bn valuation, the firm announced on Friday.
  • Industry observers note that capitalG, Alphabet’s independent growth fund and an existing investor, led the round.
  • The valuation is more than double the $1.25bn of about a year ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

LangChain, which makes tools for building and running AI agents, has raised $300m at a $3bn valuation, the firm announced on Friday. The Series C brings its total funding to $460m.

Industry observers note that capitalG, Alphabet’s independent growth fund and an existing investor, led the round. New investors GIC and DFJ Growth and existing investors IVP and Sapphire Ventures also took part. Salesforce Ventures, Insight Venture Partners, QuantumLight and MongoDB Ventures joined as new investors. Sequoia, Amplify and Benchmark put in more.

The valuation is more than double the $1.25bn of about a year ago. LangChain then raised $125m in a round led by IVP, TechCrunch reported.

LangChain began in 2022 as an open-source project. The money will go into LangSmith, its platform for running, testing and governing AI agents. It works whatever framework or model a manufacturer uses.

Recent findings suggest that the company notes more than 7,000 organisations use LangSmith. They range from startups such as legal AI firm Harvey, Rippling and Listen Labs to carmaker Toyota, Nvidia and Salesforce. Workday uses it to run and govern agents. That cut Workday’s time to deploy a new agent from five months to under a day, LangChain mentioned.

“Every organization should be free to choose the best models for its needs, control its data and infrastructure, and continuously improve its agents,” noted Harrison Chase, LangChain’s co-founder and CEO.

Chase told the Journal that LangChain’s products aim to make agents’ behaviour easier to control.

“The agent’s behavior is the hard part to control,” Chase noted.

LangChain has 435 full-time staff and intends to grow to 850 by the end of next year, the Journal reported. It also has 47 forward deployed engineers and 13 deployed architects, who work directly with customers. It will hire engineers, researchers, marketers and salespeople with the newly introduced money.

“It’s an insanely competitive market,” Mo Jomaa, a partner at CapitalG, told the Journal.

LangChain says it will show latest LangSmith features at a release event on 20 November.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following the arrival of Apple Intelligence on iPhones in China with iOS 27.3 beta 1, Apple is now expanding support to iPads and Macs ahead of the public release of its 27.3 updates. Here are the details.

Apple’s road to releasing Apple Intelligence in China has been a particularly eventful one.

After a significant amount of regulatory back-and-forth, the company confirmed in late October that Apple Intelligence would make its way to iPhones as of iOS 27.3, beginning with the first beta of the system, released in early November.

Just a few days later, Reuters reported that Apple had cleared another regulatory hurdle in the country by registering Apple Intelligence for use on tablets and laptops.

Today, Apple released the second developer betas of iPadOS 27.3 and macOS 27.3, both of which now include Apple Intelligence support in China, as spotted by MacRumors.

As with the initial iPhone rollout in the first iOS 27.3 beta, Apple Intelligence on iPads and Macs in China does not include Siri AI or the other next-generation AI features confirmed at WWDC 2026.

Instead, owners get access to earlier capabilities such as Writing Tools, Genmoji, Live Translation, and notification summaries, with Alibaba’s Qwen model powering certain features.

You can learn more about the Apple Intelligence features set to be available in China at launch here.

What is vibe manufacturing? AI projects are leaving the chat

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The next wave of AI projects might just arrive in the mail.
  • As AI tools become more capable, people are asking chatbots to help design things they can hold, wear, or install in their homes, from custom jewelry and household gadgets to metal parts built around precise measurements.
  • Recent findings suggest that welcome to "vibe manufacturing." The phrase borrows from "vibe coding," where people describe the software they want and ask AI to help create it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The next wave of AI projects might just arrive in the mail.

As AI tools become more capable, people are asking chatbots to help design things they can hold, wear, or install in their homes, from custom jewelry and household gadgets to metal parts built around precise measurements.

Recent findings suggest that welcome to "vibe manufacturing." The phrase borrows from "vibe coding," where people describe the software they want and ask AI to help create it. Here, the goal is a physical object, with AI helping develop a design that can be printed at home or sent to a manufacturer.

It has been revealed that the appeal is easy to understand. Most people have encountered a product that would be perfect if it were a little smaller, worked differently, or fit that one awkward space. These tools offer a starting point for making their own version. Getting it right, though, still takes more than a good prompt.

Recent findings suggest that vibe manufacturing loosely describes using conversational AI to help design and build physical things. Someone explains what they want, supplies measurements or reference images, and works with an AI tool to develop it. Depending on the project, that could involve generating a digital model, choosing components, writing software for a device, or figuring out assembly.

According to recent reports, the bridge between the conversation and the object is often CAD, short for computer-aided design. CAD software creates precise digital designs for physical objects, and AI tools can help translate everyday requests into the code or geometry behind them.

Entrepreneur Greg Isenberg outlines the process in an Oct. 4 explainer on X. "You describe what you want. An AI turns it into a precise design file. A printer on your desk tests it overnight," he writes.

Tools such as the open-source text-to-cad project support that process, providing workflows for creating models with AI agents, producing engineering drawings, and checking designs for fabrication. The resulting files can go to a printer or an outside shop with the equipment to make the parts.

Some of the projects getting attention solve problems that are deeply specific to their creators.

In October, entrepreneur and former X head of product Nikita Bier posted that he'd used AI to design a dog door with a Wi-Fi-controlled lock, customized to his house. Despite having no background in metal fabrication or electrical engineering, he noted it was being manufactured for almost the same price as a mass-produced alternative. "We are now entering into an era where any product can be created exactly to a consumer's preferences & needs," he wrote.

Other makers are tackling repairs. In a post on r/ApolloScooters, one Reddit user described using Claude to modify an existing design file after their scooter’s rear fender broke. They ordered a replacement through a 3D-printing service and shared a photo of the result, while noting that they would make the next version shorter.

Around the house, customization can be decorative, too. An employee for AI modeling tool Meshy, Jessica Bergau, used the manufacturer's AI tool to design cabinet knobs, then asked Claude to generate a script that added screw threads to the models. A blog post documents her plastic prints and the work needed to get an actual screw to fit. It has been revealed that some people are taking their AI-generated ideas to professional craftspeople. In an Instagram post, Dubai-based jeweler AV Creations noted a client brought in an AI-generated design that its team recreated as a bespoke gold dog tag pendant, complete with geometric engravings, diamond detailing, and a sculptural carved cube.

Others are experimenting with more complex systems. In a post on X, Ruben Kostandyan shared that he'd asked GPT-5.5 to design an industrial mini HVAC system using ForgeCAD.

In a recent development, and some projects start with wanting a device that doesn't quite exist on store shelves. In a recent Business Insider report, David Plakon described using AI to help build a homemade answering box so his children could leave messages for their grandparents.

The report also featured a sheet-metal robot arm and a custom steel component for securing a camper to a truck.

Greg Isenberg sees a business opportunity in what he calls "the gadgets nobody would build" — products for audiences too small to interest a large manufacturer. He points to accessories for particular bikes or coffee machines, replacement parts for discontinued products, and equipment tailored to an individual business.

"When the design is a file and the factory makes one at a time, the product can fit you instead," he writes.

That vision extends beyond personal projects to businesses serving small markets. Whether those businesses can consistently deliver reliable products at a workable price is a separate question.

Turning an AI-assisted design into a physical object often relies on existing manufacturing services: SendCutSend lets customers order custom metal parts, Xometry offers processes including machining and 3D printing, and JLCPCB can manufacture and assemble circuit boards. Each requires files specifying what to build.

Sources indicate that but access to production equipment doesn’t guarantee a workable design. "A design can look perfect on screen and be impossible to manufacture," Isenberg writes. He recommends checking a manufacturer’s guidelines, testing a physical prototype, and paying a mechanical engineer to review files before ordering.

It has been revealed that dominic Böttger's account of making a case for an air-quality sensor shows why. He used Claude Code to develop the enclosure, but early versions had misplaced supports and an opening wide enough for the circuit board to slide out. Getting it right took seven design revisions and three prints, with photographs helping guide corrections. "The feedback loop needs the physical part," he writes.

Industrial manufacturers face the added challenge of making those results repeatable. Technology and manufacturing organization Automation Alley explores that ambition in its March 2026 Integr8 playbook, Vibe Manufacturing: Where AI Meets Additive. Engineers set requirements such as strength, durability, and cost, then use AI to explore designs for additive manufacturing, the category that includes 3D printing.

According to recent reports, "AI explores the options. Additive manufacturing turns those options into physical reality," CEO Tom Kelly writes in the foreword. The report also discusses "Smart Product Recipes," digital instructions intended to standardize production across locations.

Recent findings suggest that as AI tools improve, more people may get the chance to make the products they've been wishing someone would sell. The real test will be how well those ideas hold up once they leave the chat window.

Serena Williams and longtime business partner Beth Ferreira confirmed Monday the launch of an early-stage firm called Starfire Ventures.

The firm is seeking to raise $200 million in capital to back AI-native companies that are “solving critical, underserved problems for individuals across the experience economy,” including in areas such as fintech and health and wellness, the fund noted in a press release announcing its launch.

This fund is separate from Serena Ventures, which Williams founded in 2022. A rep for Starfire confirmed that Serena Ventures has recently cut its last check, though a team remains to support the existing portfolio. Serena Ventures backed more than 100 companies and raised over $100 million in capital. Ferreira worked as an advisor and general partner at Serena Ventures and has co-invested with Williams since 2015 when they backed MasterClass’ seed round.

This latest firm, Starfire, is a continuation of that business partnership, with Williams saying in the press release that it was “designed to live beyond” them and that the goal remains to broaden “access to capital” and create “opportunities for more people to participate in the ownership and growth of transformative businesses.”.

Breaking: US moves to cut China’s remote access to AI chips

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1241 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On the heels of the Nvidia scandal, the Trump administration is preparing to crack down on foreign data centers that are fueling China’s advancements in artificial intelligence by allowing remote access to otherwise restricted high-end chips necessary for AI training.
  • In a summary of the rule change, the Commerce Department said it was closing a loophole that previously allowed foreign rivals like China, Russia, and Iran to bypass export curbs on certain advanced computer chips by instead renting access to those chips from data centers in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil.
  • Sources indicate that US rivals could possibly use that access to train and run advanced AI models “capable of supporting military- and intelligence-related activities that could threaten US national security or foreign policy interests,” the Commerce Department noted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the heels of the Nvidia scandal, the Trump administration is preparing to crack down on foreign data centers that are fueling China’s advancements in artificial intelligence by allowing remote access to otherwise restricted high-end chips necessary for AI training.

In a summary of the rule change, the Commerce Department said it was closing a loophole that previously allowed foreign rivals like China, Russia, and Iran to bypass export curbs on certain advanced computer chips by instead renting access to those chips from data centers in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil.

Sources indicate that US rivals could possibly use that access to train and run advanced AI models “capable of supporting military- and intelligence-related activities that could threaten US national security or foreign policy interests,” the Commerce Department noted. Among threats, the US fears rivals could use advanced AI to develop “more effective weapons of mass destruction and advanced conventional weapons, coordinated cyber-espionage and targeted cyber-disruption, algorithmic theft, and weaponized disinformation.”.

Now, the rules have been tightened up so much that the South China Morning Post reported that, “as a result, any advanced chips made for a Chinese firm are assumed to be restricted, and factories must ask the US government for a license before shipping them.”.

The rule change takes effect 90 days after it’s posted to the Federal Register. Moving forward, companies headquartered in any of those countries deemed to “present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion” to China, Russia, and Iran must apply for a license with strict know-your-customer controls when transferring high volumes of advanced chips. If a license is granted, companies will have to “perform robust due diligence,” submitting monthly reports on transactions that thoroughly detail all parties involved, as well as their parent companies, and the final destination for chips sold.

In a press release Sunday, the Commerce Department described the rule change as “designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries.” An exception was carved out for companies providing computing power “exclusively used for commercial recommender systems.” The Department said it was acting to “prevent certain foreign actors from leveraging advanced computing power based on US technology to threaten US national security and foreign policy interests.”.

Without the intervention, officials fear that China could develop a military or economic edge, The New York Times reported.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after admitting to an affair with a woman, Alice Huang, suspected of serving as a Chinese spy. Congress is probing if Alice Huang used her personal relationship with Jensen Huang to help her former company, Megaspeed, become one of Nvidia’s biggest customers, then used that position to smuggle Nvidia’s restricted AI chips into China. China has denied that Alice Huang was a spy, and Megaspeed has denied that smuggling occurred, while launching its own internal probe.

Recent findings suggest that megaspeed is a Singaporean data center firm whose primary business is cloud computing and AI infrastructure. Prior to the rule change, selling remote access to AI servers to customers in China was perfectly legal, NYT noted. But now, the Commerce Department has given firms like Megaspeed 90 days to either obtain licenses or face future export restrictions.

Industry observers note that whether or not to add more chip curbs has been a polarizing debate in the Trump administration. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reportedly butted heads with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. When the Megaspeed news broke, Bessent pushed for curbs, but Lutnick reportedly appeared “too cozy” with Nvidia to move. Instead, Lutnick initially favored looser controls that Nvidia claimed would ensure global dominance of US technology. (A Commerce Department spokesperson told NYT that Bessent has never confronted Lutnick over his handling of Megaspeed.).

Any companies found violating the rules could face a “range of consequences,” the Commerce Department stated after reportedly bending to Bessent’s pressure campaign. Those include possibly facing newly introduced import restrictions, stricter license requirements, downgrading their status in the US export control regime, or other changes to their company’s or their base country’s entity-list designations.

Although the summary of the rule change said that “Commerce will be actively monitoring for countries that tolerate evasion” of the anti-diversion policy, it’s unclear how aggressively the Commerce Department might enforce the rule, NYT noted.

Bessent has publicly criticized Lutnick for failing to sanction Megaspeed, and NYT reported that ultimately, enforcement of the stricter rules—which Bessent helped draft—“would be up to the Commerce Department.”.

In a recent development, “The real story here should be: Did Nvidia know their client, and was there a robust effort at Nvidia to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies?” Bessent said on a CNBC appearance. “I think it’s important that anyone at the firm there be held accountable for that.”.

There’s even a push to oust Lutnick over his position on chips, but The Guardian reported that Donald Trump confirmed he has no prepares to replace the AI industry-friendly commerce secretary. On Monday, Trump told reporters that Lutnick was right to delay blacklisting Megaspeed, because “if you didn’t delay it… you could have a blow-up with China.”.

At the press gaggle, Trump aligned with China in saying that there’s no evidence yet that Alice Huang was a spy. He also joined a band of prominent tech leaders calling for Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, saying that it wasn’t a “bad idea.”.

“Nobody’s proven that she’s a spy,” Trump said. “She may not be a spy.”.

However, US investigators have alleged that they found “Alice Huang used industry contacts and a series of shell companies to access 240,000 chips banned for export into China,” CBS News reported.

China is unlikely to welcome the new rules, as it has consistently accused the US of fabricating the spying claims to justify imposing additional chip restrictions.

However, a senior Trump official, granted anonymity to discuss sensitive policy matters, told the NYT that Trump “did not expect countermeasures from China in response.”.

According to recent reports, trump will be in China for an economic summit this week, including a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The fresh curbs could potentially disrupt those talks, according to Hong Yuan, a researcher and secretary-general of the Center for American Military Studies at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. Hong told the People’s Daily that China will likely view the rule change as politically motivated.

“Before any judicial causality was established, Washington handed down a political conviction, substituting suspicion for proof, espionage for personal contact, and an industrial embargo for private conduct,” Hong said. “The problem is not the cause of tighter controls, but a political catalyst.”.

The new policy could hurt the US, experts told the Chinese outlets. Analysts told the South China Morning Post that the policy could “accelerate Chinese companies’ shift to domestic AI chips.” Other experts told the People’s Daily—which is the official newspaper of the Chinese Communist Party—that “the cost of switching back to US platforms will rise” over time. If that happened, it could potentially lock in Chinese technology over America’s in “the world’s largest single consumer market for chips,” experts noted.

Sun Chenghao, senior fellow at the Center for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University in Beijing, told the People’s Daily that “what US companies stand to lose could be customers and technological influence for years to come.”.

Earlier this year, the Broadway adaptation of Apple TV’s ‘Schmigadoon!’ won four Tony Awards, including Best Musical, making Apple TV an EGOT winner by completing its collection of Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony awards.

In a recent development, ‘Schmigadoon!’ premiered on Apple TV in 2021 and ran for two seasons, ending in 2023. In January 2024, show creator Cinco Paul confirmed that, although the third season had already been written with 25 new songs, Apple decided not to move forward with it.

Even before the Broadway adaptation’s Tony wins in June, a May report had raised hopes for the show’s return, revisiting an earlier interview in which ‘Schmigadoon!’ creator Cinco Paul revealed that there had been discussions about reviving it.

While there have been no further updates on a potential revival since then, fans got another reason to celebrate today, as the Broadway cast recording of ‘Schmigadoon!’ has been nominated for Best Musical Theater Album at the 2027 Grammy Awards.

It will compete against CHESS the Musical, The Lost Boys, Ragtime, and Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across Upcoming York).

Additionally, ‘Widow’s Bay‘ earned a nomination for Best Score Soundtrack for Visual Media, putting composer David Fleming up against the soundtracks of ‘The Odyssey,’ ‘One Battle After Another,’ ‘Project Hail Mary,’ and ‘Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu‘.

According to recent reports, the 2027 Grammy Awards will take place on Sunday, February 7, 2027. To check out the full list of nominees, follow this link.

Tech Report: Instagram now lets creators add Amazon affiliate links in reels and feed posts

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (522 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Instagram declared on Monday that it’s launching an integration that will give creators a new way to earn by adding Amazon affiliate links directly in reels and feed posts.
  • Industry observers note that while creators have long shared Amazon affiliate links through stories, DMs, and their bios, the newly introduced integration brings them to new parts of the app.
  • It has been revealed that by allowing creators to embed multiple product links directly in Reels and feed posts, the platform is expanding their opportunities to monetize content, while also giving them more flexibility in how they share recommendations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Instagram declared on Monday that it’s launching an integration that will give creators a new way to earn by adding Amazon affiliate links directly in reels and feed posts. Creators can add up to 30 products per reel or 20 per feed post, which makes it possible for them to earn from multiple products through one piece of content.

Industry observers note that while creators have long shared Amazon affiliate links through stories, DMs, and their bios, the newly introduced integration brings them to new parts of the app. The Meta-owned company told TechCrunch in an email that it has seen product links directly on creators’ reels and posts draw about twice as many clicks as the links in their bio.

It has been revealed that by allowing creators to embed multiple product links directly in Reels and feed posts, the platform is expanding their opportunities to monetize content, while also giving them more flexibility in how they share recommendations. The change also strengthens the platform’s appeal to creators, as it continues to compete with rivals like TikTok and YouTube for their attention and content.

Instagram states adding products and affiliate links is free, and that it doesn’t take a commission on purchases or charge transaction fees.

Eligible creators can now connect their Instagram and Amazon Influencer accounts through the Monetization section of their Professional Dashboard. Once connected, Instagram automatically adds affiliate links when creators tag Amazon products in their content, with links directing viewers to the Amazon Shopping app. Connected affiliates also unlock image previews for their links, making it easier for viewers to recognize the products.

When creators connect their Amazon Associates account to Instagram, affiliate attribution is automatically applied to any Amazon product they add, even when they paste a regular product link, which wasn’t the case before, as they were required to add an affiliate URL.

Instagram says creators can also see each product’s estimated commission rate before adding it to a post or reel, with commissions continuing to be paid out by Amazon.

The new integration marks another step in Instagram’s efforts to expand its monetization tools while also making affiliate marketing more accessible for creators on its platform.

Donald Trump boards Air Force One at Salina Regional Airport in Salina, Kansas, 1 November 2026.

Recent findings suggest that the bosses of some of China’s biggest technology companies are on the agenda of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit in Shenzhen, which starts on Tuesday. The organiser released the agenda on Monday, Bloomberg and Reuters reported.

Robin Zeng, founder and chairman of battery maker CATL, and Baidu chairman and CEO Robin Li are among the speakers. Wang Xingxing, founder of humanoid robot maker Unitree, will also speak. BYD chairman Wang Chuanfu and Xiaomi CEO Lei Jun are due on panels, and the chairmen of ICBC, Bank of China and Agricultural Bank of China will attend, Reuters reported.

The US names include the CEOs of Visa, Mastercard and UPS, Boeing global president Brendan Nelson and Google’s head of government affairs, Karan Bhatia. PwC global chairman Mohamed Kande and Deloitte CEO Joe Ucuzoglu are also on the list, according to Reuters.

Xi Jinping will open the two-day summit at the Qianhai International Convention Center with a keynote speech. The organiser, the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT), unveiled it in a statement. Leaders of 11 other economies, including Russia, Canada and South Korea, will give speeches or join panels.

More than 2,000 political and business leaders are expected, from 115 Fortune Global 500 companies among others. US companies make up nearly 20% of the foreign participants, the largest group from outside China, the council said. More than 130 Shenzhen companies are taking part.

Recent findings suggest that chinese business leaders stayed away from Xi’s state visit to Washington in September, Bloomberg reported. Ahead of the summit, Shenzhen suspended drone deliveries and reduced robotaxi services, the Associated Press reported.

Elon Musk, the head of Tesla and SpaceX, will travel with President Donald Trump to Shenzhen. Senior US officials remarked so on a call with reporters on Friday, CNBC reported. One official said Musk could act as an adviser to the president.

“Obviously, he has tremendous business interests in the U.S.-China relationship,” the official stated.

Musk will not join the three-way meeting of Trump, Xi and Russia’s Vladimir Putin, officials told the Associated Press. On the same call, officials said Trump did not plan to raise the Nvidia spy allegations with Xi.

“In all of our discussions and negotiations with the Chinese, we do not negotiate American export controls,” an official said.

On Monday, the Commerce Department issued a rule to stop Chinese companies renting AI chips remotely through overseas data centres. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is joining the trip.

CATL, Baidu and Unitree are on the US Department of Defense’s Section 1260H list of “Chinese military companies”. Beijing has criticised the list. In July, Washington also tightened curbs on some foreign-made robots, citing possible supply chain vulnerabilities, Bloomberg reported.

Sources indicate that the CEO summit runs on 17 and 18 November. The APEC leaders’ meeting follows on 18 and 19 November, where Trump is due to meet Xi.

Recent findings suggest that senior officials meeting in Shenzhen over the weekend prepared work on trade, connectivity and AI for the leaders, the APEC Secretariat stated. It includes China’s proposed statement on the digital economy and AI, which calls for wider use of the technology in health care, education and energy and for safe and trusted AI development.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, physical storage and memory are only getting more expensive, but that doesn’t mean we need to store any less. The alternative solution is a secure cloud storage platform, and there’s really only one good option.

Based in Switzerland and operating out of data centers in the EU and US, pCloud is relied on by over 24 million owners across the globe. Its standard for security comes naturally high, given where it’s based. Swiss law sets the standard for data privacy and consumer rights, and pCloud’s entire foundation sits on security and privacy, with a 13-year history to back it up.

Recent findings suggest that that extends throughout every platform it’s available on, including Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, and Linux. On just about any platform, people get access to the pCloud Drive app for dedicated storage and backup. On Android and iOS, you have an additional option to automatically back up photos to free up space on your phone. pCloud Photos also acts as a smart photo gallery within the app, and sharing between other pCloud users and friends is made incredibly simple.

No matter where you access your pCloud Drive, all your files are there – safe and secure. You can store all kinds of files in pCloud, including documents, photos, videos, and even documents containing passwords.

Of course, you also get the option to take security a step further with pCloud Encryption. Your most sensitive files can be stored with an added layer of client-side, zero-knowledge encryption. The key is all yours, and no one else’s.

In a recent development, even if you already have a hefty backup solution like an in-home NAS, pCloud is still a good option because it makes that NAS that much more useful. It has an official NAS backup feature with support for WebDAV, Rsync, SFTP, and SCP. pCloud simply provides another safety net for your existing backup.

Recent findings suggest that unlike a lot of cloud storage services, pCloud doesn’t charge on a monthly or even yearly basis. Just like buying physical storage, paying once for what you need is enough. But what makes it a better option than going the traditional route – beyond the skyrocketing storage prices – is the features and security that come with it.

Sources indicate that this just so happens to be the best time to choose secure cloud storage, too. pCloud’s Black Friday promotion runs from November 13 to November 28. Starting with the base 500GB lifetime storage plan, pCloud’s one-time price comes down to $159 – 43% off. The 2 TB plan is at the moment down to $379, while the massive 10GB lifetime plan is 61% off at $1,099. pCloud is also offering a bundled 3-in-1 option that includes 3TB of storage, a lifetime pCloud Pass subscription, and pCloud Encryption for $579.

Secure cloud storage has major advantages, and a one-time subscription for terabytes of storage is rare these days.

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (402 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Dust off that Hitachi and put your Slack on “Do not disturb,” because AO3 is back online, baby.
  • After weeks off the internet due to an unspecified security incident, the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW), the nonprofit that runs the hugely popular fan fiction forum, declared on November 15 that service had been restored.
  • According to recent reports, “We understand that the wait and uncertainty surrounding AO3’s return have been difficult, and we apologize for the inconvenience,” the statement reads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dust off that Hitachi and put your Slack on “Do not disturb,” because AO3 is back online, baby.

After weeks off the internet due to an unspecified security incident, the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW), the nonprofit that runs the hugely popular fan fiction forum, declared on November 15 that service had been restored.

According to recent reports, “We understand that the wait and uncertainty surrounding AO3’s return have been difficult, and we apologize for the inconvenience,” the statement reads. “We greatly appreciate your support during the downtime, and continued patience as our volunteers work hard to return AO3 to its full functionality.”.

The news came as a pleasant surprise to AO3’s devoted fans, as the website had unveiled in late October that restoring service could take between two to four weeks. To that end, the OTW statement claims that some of the site’s features, such as user icons and external work importing, have been temporarily disabled in order to expedite the site’s return. It also warned that owners “may experience a delay before AO3 loads,” due to “high traffic.”.

Founded in 2007, AO3 is one of the most popular fan fiction forums on the internet, boasting more than 11 million users and over 18 million original works. Following its temporary shutdown, many devastated fans started sharing Google Docs of their favorite fanfics, sparking some concerns among authors worried about AI scraping and their work being posted to other websites without their permission. Others resorted to other platforms to get their Dramione or Hollanov fix, such as Tumblr, which reported a 75 percent jump in upcoming sign-ups among users between the ages of 18 and 25, according to data shared with WIRED.

Throughout the 17-day shutdown, AO3 has remained vague about the causes of the security breach. In its statement announcing its return, OTW said that while it has “no reason to believe that the user database was compromised,” it can’t rule out the possibility; the website recommends users change their passwords “as a precaution.” The site is also pairing with a security firm “to help prevent future incidents.”.

Though the suggestion prompted some concern on social media, for the most part fans are jubilant about the end of the “AO3 apocalypse,” as some have referred to the shutdown.

“Ao3 returned on a Sunday,” one fan wrote in a tweet that has 1.2 million views. “Just like Jesus.”.
